more.title: Starting upstream: Rethinking how public health supports young people
more.summary: When GCH assistant professor Rochelle Davidson Mhonde began working with adolescent survivors of sexual violence, she saw the ripple effects of their trauma: depression, anxiety, substance use and other health challenges. "Survivors often know what support they need to heal. But when they don't receive it, the consequences can compound far beyond the original harm," she said.

more.title: Fashion startup Atorie raises $9.5M to bring consumers luxury goods without the markup
more.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
more.summary: Shoppers can visit the Atorie website and buy handbags or clothes made from the same material — and coming from the same factory — that manufacturers use in high-end goods.

more.title: This former PG&E engineer is building a ‘Google Maps for the underground’
more.author: Sean O'Kane
more.summary: The startup just raised a $26 million Series A to grow its customer base and help reduce red tape for utility and construction work.

more.title: Evolution favors flatter paths when fitness outcomes are equal, study finds
more.summary: A surprising discovery by Technion researchers sheds new light on the dynamics of evolution. Published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the study shows that when an organism has several evolutionary paths available with equal fitness, the path it follows is not necessarily chosen at random.

more.title: As electric two-wheelers gain a foothold, Belgian startup Any bets on cargo space
more.author: Anna Heim
more.summary: Launched by Belgian startup Any, LUV1 is a modular electric motorcycle with 120 liters of cargo space that can be used to carry bags, work equipment, or even pets.

more.title: NASA Invites Media to Turkey Artemis Accords Signing Ceremony
more.author: Jennifer M. Dooren
more.summary: Turkey will sign the Artemis Accords during a ceremony at 2:30 p.m. EDT Monday, Aug. 31, at NASA Headquarters in Washington, becoming the 71st country signatory. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will host Turkish Minister of Industry and Technology Mehmet Fatih Kacır for the ceremony, together with U.S. Department of State officials. This event is in person only. […]

more.title: Specific cover crops may help attract insects that target harmful pests
more.summary: Different cover crops may affect how plants defend themselves against pests—including by attracting more insects that eat harmful caterpillars—according to a new study led by researchers at Penn State's College of Agricultural Sciences.

more.title: Vehicle-mounted spectroscopy system detects methane in real time
more.summary: Researchers have developed a vehicle-mounted spectroscopy system that can reliably detect methane in real time while driving. Using a moving vehicle to detect methane could make it easier to locate hidden methane emissions across large areas.

more.title: Socure Secures $156M at $5.2B Valuation, Acquires AI Fraud Investigation Startup Fravity
more.author: Judy Rider
more.summary: Identity verification and fraud prevention company Socure announced Thursday that it raised $156 million in a strategic growth investment valuing it at $5.2 billion. The Incline Village, Nevada-based company also says it is acquiring agentic AI startup Fravity, which will be incorporated into its RiskOS platform as RiskOS_Agents.

more.title: Discovery reveals rapid pathways to complex aromatic molecules in space
more.summary: A team of researchers led by the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa Department of Chemistry has uncovered a faster way large carbon-based molecules may form in space, helping solve a long-standing mystery about how some of the building blocks of the universe grow.

more.title: Study reveals inter-city collaboration on emission reduction boosts sustainability performance
more.summary: With Hong Kong recently recording record-breaking high temperatures, extreme weather has once again raised public awareness of global warming and emission-reduction measures. A large-scale international study led by The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) has revealed that intercity collaboration on emission reduction can improve overall sustainability performance by more than 10%.

more.title: Scientists tested 212 plant-based meat alternatives. Every one contained fungal toxins
more.summary: Every one of 212 plant-based meat alternatives and drinks tested in the UK contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin, though concentrations remained below recommended EU guideline levels. Researchers say the bigger question is whether regularly eating large amounts of these foods could lead to potentially concerning cumulative exposure over time.

more.title: Short, intense storms gain intensity across Hawaiʻi
more.summary: While long-term data show that Hawaiʻi is getting drier overall, short, intense downpours that cause sudden, dangerous flash floods are getting stronger on the islands, according to a new study by researchers at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

more.title: Heat-tolerant corals may be more vulnerable to disease
more.summary: Corals that partner with heat-tolerant algae may be better equipped to survive warming oceans—but that resilience comes with an unexpected trade-off, according to a new study from Boston University published in Science Advances.

more.title: Mixture of traditional edible plants inhibits fungus growth in corn, study shows
more.summary: Fungal contamination in stored grain across sub-Saharan Africa causes major post-harvest losses and severe public health risks, costing billions of dollars annually, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). High humidity, warm temperatures and inadequate storage facilities can drive mold proliferation and toxin production in staple crops such as corn and sorghum.

more.title: How much of a threat do heat waves pose to nuclear plants?
more.author: Alexander Kaufman
more.summary: Europe’s increasingly hot summers come with a worrying trend. The air conditioning that the continent long eschewed as an American indulgence is becoming a necessity, and some of the nuclear reactors needed to run those cooling units are tapping out right as thermometers spike. This summer was especially bad: The…

more.title: Bird flu detected in dead dolphin in South Australia
more.summary: H5N1 bird flu has been detected in a dead dolphin in South Australia, state officials said Friday, the first case of its kind in the country.

more.title: Fast but error-prone AI assists in solving a decades-old fluid mechanics problem in five weeks
more.summary: An AI assistant helped University of Colorado Boulder researchers solve a mathematical problem that had challenged their lab for a year and a half, though it made subtle errors along the way. The breakthrough could improve how scientists study nanoparticles—tiny particles about 1,000 times thinner than a human hair—but it reveals both the promise and limitations of AI as a scientific research partner.

more.title: Satellite images show bedrock and glacier collapsed on Nepal-China border, then rivers flooded
more.summary: As rescue teams searched for missing people following catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-China border, Earth scientists reviewed satellite imagery for clues to the cause and assessed the devastation.

more.title: America's big but uncertain gas boom
more.author: Dan McCarthy
more.summary: See more from Canary Media’s ​“Chart of the Week” column . Developers are planning to build an enormous amount of natural gas-fired power plants in the U.S., fueled in large part by the AI boom. The expansion is a serious threat to the nation’s decarbonization efforts — but because so much gas development remains…

more.author: Shrishti Bisht
more.summary: EV maker Ola Electric has launched its new S1Z escooter range, powered by the company’s locally developed 46-series lithium iron…

more.title: ASTRID traces 13.5 billion years of black hole and galaxy evolution
more.summary: In dark skies at night, distant starlight twinkles and speaks to vast cosmic histories almost as old as time itself. New data from instruments such as NASA's James Webb Space Telescope are helping astrophysicists probe deep cosmic mysteries, including the evolution of black holes and galaxies.

more.title: Why did 1,000 world citizens bury their underpants?
more.author: Jennifer Ouellette
more.summary: Study: Land use is the biggest factor in determining decomposition rates of organic cotton underpants.

more.title: Scientists tracked 4,500 animals and found a surprising human effect
more.summary: Scientists tracking thousands of animals found that our physical presence can reshape where wildlife moves and lives, sometimes as strongly as roads, cities, and other human development. Because different species reacted in very different ways, conservation efforts may need to become much more targeted.
